scope: Fresh source-only re-verification of 4eaadb01 and 229e599e atop e15aac6a and b02b04ba; D84/D86 native Settings persistence harness only.

findings.evidence: tests/browser/settings-desktop-native-acceptance.mjs state() distinguishes pairSaveError from pairForgetError; refusal/retry predicates for Forget use pairForgetError (roughly lines 94-95, 575-600). Matches SettingsView.tsx:626.

When pair input is absent, entry is explicitly not_applicable, and the separate Forget branch records unverified when its control is absent; final report.status becomes partial if any case is unverified (lines 558-607, 691). SettingsView.tsx:559-566 and 610-629 couple those controls to transport, so absent pair entry also hides Forget for native transport; HTTP exposes both.

storageCensus hashes key/value pairs for both storage areas; reset refusal requires every prior key retained and every prior value identical (lines 105-160, 635-652). Successful reset checks no unexplained prior entries remain and requires removal of its explicit session fixture (lines 673-685). Values and keys are reported as salted digests/categories, not raw data.

state() now reads chrome.storage.local.get(null) (line 73), while the injected wrapper only faults targeted reads whose argument includes PORT_KEY; storage fault helper targets arrays containing the key or exact-key reads (settings-desktop-storage-faults.mjs targets()). The observer cannot consume that held operation.

verdict_a_acceptance.status: PARTIAL — source establishes intended cases and honest partial reporting; native acceptance remains unverified
evidence: Port and pair operations use actual Settings UI controls and Chrome storage; reset compares actual local/session contents before and after the refusal and retry.
No native run receipt/runtime execution was reviewed or run in this lane, so this does not prove the handlers work in Chrome or close D84/D86.
limits: Scope is bounded persistence and ordering; it does not prove a healthy desktop-engine connection, full desktop discovery, every Settings control, or all inventory T43-T51 behavior.
Census proves preservation/removal of keys present at baseline plus the owned session fixture; it is not a general census of keys created after the baseline.
